action.content: Write a joke about anarchists in Tulsa in 3 sections. Mark the beginning of each section with SECTION X.
action.label: context

action.content:
SECTION 1
In 1921 Tulsa, a group of self-proclaimed anarchists decided to hold a town hall meeting to discuss the abolition of property rights and the establishment of a communal society. They gathered in the basement of a local church, bringing nothing but a few crates of dynamite and a very optimistic attitude.

SECTION 2
The meeting was interrupted by the arrival of the Greenwood District's finest, who were confused by the lack of a formal agenda and the sudden appearance of a sign reading "Everything is Free." The anarchists explained that they had come to liberate the city from the concept of ownership, but the crowd simply asked if they could borrow a cup of sugar, to which the anarchists replied, "Only if you promise to never own the spoon again."

SECTION 3
Just as the debate reached a fever pitch about the philosophical implications of shared resources, the wind blew a stray match from a nearby lantern into a pile of discarded newspapers. The anarchists immediately cheered, shouting, "Finally, a spontaneous combustion of the old order!" while the rest of Tulsa watched in horror as the basement began to fill with smoke, realizing that in a city built on order, even chaos needs a little more planning than just lighting a match.||
